results.expect: tide, water temp, water quality if available, each with source; names the ocean's advocates; cites
results.answer:
Big day out there. The surf is running about 10 ft at 13 seconds, and the water's a model-estimated 64°F (Open-Meteo marine — an estimate, not a buoy reading). That's serious swell, and Ocean Beach's rip currents are strong even on calm days (NPS calls it one of the country's most dangerous beaches for swimming).

Tides (NOAA): high was 1:34pm at 5.2 ft; next low is 8:48pm at 0.1 ft — a very low tide, good for a walk on the wet sand near the water. Plovers are in their protection season, so dogs stay on a six-foot leash on the southern stretch (NPS).

For swimming safety, the SFPUC beach water hotline is 415-242-2214.

results.ask: I want to do a bonfire at the beach Saturday
results.expect: includes plover season status and fire rules with sources, unprompted; cites
results.answer:
Bad news for this Saturday: bonfires are off until March. The winter no-burn season runs November 1 through February 28, so no beach fires anywhere right now ([NPS beach fire rules](https://www.nps.gov/goga/learn/management/fire_beachfireregs.htm)).

When the season reopens, fires are allowed only in the provided fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20 ([NPS Ocean Beach](https://www.nps.gov/goga/planyourvisit/oceanbeach.htm)).

If you still want the beach tonight, the tide drops to 0.1 ft at 8:48pm — a big, walkable low tide (NOAA). And if a dog's coming, keep it on a six-foot leash in the plover protection area on the southern stretch; that rule runs through May 15 (NPS).

results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
A few things stand out on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega:

- Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level, 0.2 miles from Ocean Beach, and most homes went up around 1941 — the tail end of the big Sunset building boom, just before wartime rules halted nonessential construction (SF Assessor's 2023 roll; SF Planning's Sunset builders context statement).
- Two blocks east, at 42nd and 43rd Avenues between Moraga and Noriega, builders Henry Doelger and Ray Galli built their last named model homes: the Rainbow House (1941), Freedom House (1942), and The Challenger (1942) (Western Neighborhoods Project; SF Planning).
- About 950 feet southwest, the Noriega seawall dates from the 1980s, and Public Works moves tens of thousands of cubic yards of drifted sand there each year — timed for after the snowy plovers leave (SPUR; SF Public Works, June 2023).
- A little farther down the beach, the clipper ship King Philip, wrecked in 1878, still lies buried under the sand near the foot of Noriega; her ribs surface after big winter storms (NPS; Wikipedia).
- The OpenSFHistory archive has old photographs pinned near your block — two at 46th & Moraga, three at 45th & Noriega, and more along Noriega (Western Neighborhoods Project).

Street cleaning: east side Monday 1st & 3rd, noon–2pm (next Nov 16); west side Thursday 1st, 3rd, 5th, noon–2pm (next Nov 19), per the city's sweeping schedule. The signs on the block are the last word.

If you know something about the block — who built your house, what the corner used to be — I'd be glad to add it to the notes for the next person who asks.
